  The outcome of checking an issue for a worktree it already has.

  status                string, one of:
    none                An issue with no worktree of its own.
    removed             A leftover that held nothing but what the base holds and files
                        git ignores, and is gone along with its branch.
    kept                A worktree that failed one of the checks and was left exactly as
                        it was; whether to throw it away is a question for the person.
  worktree_path         string (may be null)
                        worktree_path and branch are null when there was no worktree,
                        rather than empty strings: the caller branches on status and
                        reads these only after.
  branch                string (may be null)
  reason                string (may be null), one of:
                        Null unless the worktree was kept.
    locked              A worktree git holds a lock on, which somebody took on purpose.
    in_use_by_process   A worktree some process has as its working directory. Removing
                        it would kill every later command of that process.
    dirty               A worktree with anything uncommitted, untracked files included.
                        Files git ignores are not looked at.
    beyond_start_ref    A branch carrying a commit the ref a new worktree would start
                        from does not: origin/<base> where it exists, the local base
                        otherwise.
    on_origin           A branch of the same name on origin, which is work somebody
                        pushed.
    origin_unreachable  An origin that could not be asked — no remote, no network. An
                        unanswered question is not taken as a no.
